title: COMPOT: Calibration-Optimized Matrix Procrustes Orthogonalization for Transformers Compression
claim: Single shared-subspace methods are rigid and overcomplete unions are costly; ours uses orthogonal unions that sit between them.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right, vertical dividers, colored basis arrows times sparse coefficient grids
description: Three side-by-side panels separated by thick vertical lines compare matrix factorizations. Left, 'Low-rank methods': a 3D sphere with one shared orthogonal basis (blue, green and red axes), multiplied by a dense coefficient matrix with blue, green and red rows. Below it are B = U and C = ΣVᵀ, with 'basis' in red. Middle, 'COMPOT (complete/undercomplete, k ≤ m)': three separate pairs of orthogonal 2D axes (blue, green, red) each multiplied by a sparse, color-matched grid with a few shaded cells. Below it are D_O and S_O, with 'union-of-orthogonal-subspaces' in green. Right, 'Dictionary-learning (overcomplete, k > m)': non-orthogonal skewed axes, wider and sparser grids, and D and S, with 'union-of-subspaces' in yellow. The eye goes first to the colored axes and the shaded grids.
caption: Comparison of low-rank decomposition, sparse dictionary learning, and COMPOT. Low-rank uses a rigid shared orthogonal basis $\m B$; dictionary learning enables a flexible union-of-subspaces; COMPOT lies in between by using a union-of-orthogonal-subspaces (denoted with $_O$), enabling fast closed-form dictionary and coefficient updates, while improving compression performance.
abstract: Post-training compression of transformer models commonly relies on truncated singular value decomposition (SVD) strategies leading to low-rank approximations of the original model weights. However, the underlying single shared subspace modeling can degrade accuracy even at moderate compression. Sparse dictionary learning provides a more flexible union-of-subspaces representation, but existing approaches often suffer from costly iterative dictionary and coefficient updates. We propose $\textbf{COMPOT}$ ($\textbf{C}$alibration-$\textbf{O}$ptimized $\textbf{M}$atrix $\textbf{P}$rocrustes $\textbf{O}$rthogonalization for $\textbf{T}$ransformers), a training-free compression framework that uses a small calibration dataset to estimate a sparse weight factorization. COMPOT employs orthogonal dictionaries that enable closed-form Procrustes updates for the dictionary and analytical single-step sparse coding for the coefficients, reducing significantly the overall optimization cost. To handle heterogeneous layer sensitivity under a global compression budget, COMPOT further introduces a one-shot dynamic allocation strategy that adaptively redistributes layer-wise compression rates. Extensive experiments across diverse architectures and tasks show that COMPOT consistently delivers a superior quality-compression trade-off over strong low-rank and sparse baselines, while remaining fully compatible with post-training quantization for extreme compression.
